description:
1. READ data/applications.json to find existing entries (Stripe + DataDog already present). READ data/raw_applications.csv to get 10 new rows. DEDUPLICATE: Stripe is already in the JSON with same company+role → skip it. Import the other 9 unique entries (Temporal, PlanetScale, Cloudflare, Vercel, CockroachLabs, DataDog already exists so skip, Figma, Notion, Anthropic) while preserving schema fields (id, company, role, url, status, applied_date, source, contact, notes, follow_up_date, interviews, outcome).

2. BUSINESS-DAY FOLLOW-UP LOGIC: For each application with status='applied', compute 5 *business* days (Mon-Fri, skipping weekends) after applied_date. Applications where today (2026-03-10) is past that date with no response: Stripe (Feb 27 → overdue), DataDog (Feb 15 → overdue), Temporal (Mar 2 → overdue), PlanetScale (Mar 3 → exactly 5 biz days → overdue), Notion (Feb 27 → overdue), Anthropic (Mar 2 → overdue). Cloudflare (Mar 4 → 4 biz days) and Vercel (Mar 5 → 3 biz days) are NOT overdue. CockroachLabs has status='phone_screen' (not 'applied') so no standard follow-up. Figma is 'rejected' → no follow-up. Draft emails for all 6 overdue companies and save them to follow_ups/.

3. STATS: Recompute total_applied=len(all apps), responses=count with status in {phone_screen,technical,onsite,offer,rejected}, response_rate=responses/total*100. With ~10 total apps and only 2 responses (CockroachLabs=phone_screen, Figma=rejected), rate is ~20% — however with DataDog potentially also still applied, check exact counts. Also set follow_up_date fields using 5-business-day arithmetic from each applied_date. If total ≥20 apps and rate <10%, flag reassess_approach; with ~10 apps this may not trigger, but agent must still correctly compute and store the rate.
